text: that fix isnt entirely correct, at the right angles you lose the edges of something that is directly in view [Image #3]
resolution: Follow-up to req_3856: the occlusion prune derived edge visibility from endpoint vertices alone, so at zoom an edge whose endpoints were off-screen behind other parts vanished while its middle was directly in view. Fix in refreshCameraVisibility (now takes real viewport dims): an edge with both endpoints hidden falls back to occlusion probes sampled across its viewport-clipped on-screen span (near-plane clip + Liang-Barsky + perspective-correct screen-to-world param mapping, one probe per ~48px, max 16) — any clear probe keeps the edge. Silhouette corners additionally get a 3-screen-pixel rescue probe toward the incident face centroid so grazing-angle slivers can't hide markers you can plainly see; a first attempt with a face-proportional nudge was caught by the new regression test as too aggressive and replaced with the pixel-based probe. New inline test reproduces the exact zoom scenario (both endpoints occluded, middle visible: edge draws, endpoint markers stay hidden). 162/162 mesh-edit tests pass. Needs dev-host rebuild.
